messages:
deploy-bot: :rotating_light: Rolling out model v4.2.0 to prod canary group (5% traffic). tag=release/v4.2.0 weights=rb_2026_04 tokenizer=tok-v2. 

emily (support): seeing an alert spike from a customer — lots of garbled responses, tokens like \"▁���\" in outputs. 5xxs ~0.8% on canary nodes.

sara (oncall): on it. initiating quick check on canary logs. can someone grab the canary host list?

james (infra): canary hosts: canary-a03, canary-a07, canary-a09. pulling logs. tailing /var/log/redwood/infer.log now.

li (ml): if tokenizer mismatch happened we might see weird token IDs + decode errors. did the release include a tokenizer package bump? release notes mention tok-v2 but prod default is tok-v1.

carlos (sre): paging now — impact likely limited to canary but observable 5xx increase, error signature: "decode_error: invalid token 0xFF" across canary instances.

pagerduty-bot: @sara has been paged for incident INC-2026-324 (severity P1).

sara (oncall): acknowledged. switching to incident channel. quick triage: is this a model weight mismatch or tokenizer mismatch? both plausible. li, what's the minimal repro?

li (ml): repro from logs: input '\\"Hello\\"' -> model generates byte sequences that decoder tries to interpret with tok-v1 -> invalid bytes. looks like weights compiled against tok-v2 but runtime using tok-v1.

anya (pm): customer-facing — which customers affected? Emily?

emily (support): okdesk ticket #5421 — enterprise customer sees gibberish in summaries, reported ~3 minutes after deploy-bot message. only traffic routed to canary. no broad customer impact yet.

sara (oncall): mitigation options: 1) disable canary rollout flag (fast) 2) rollback model to previous stable (safer) 3) hotpatch tokenizer on canary nodes (risky). Recommend flip kill-switch first to stop further rollout and then rollback. thoughts?

james (infra): kill-switch command ready: `flagctl set rollout/model_v4_2_0_enabled false --env=prod` I can run.

li (ml): rollback command: `redwoodctl model rollback --model-name redwood-llm --to-version v4.1.9 --env prod` Will need ~60s to pull weights. If we flip flag it's immediate stop for new canary assignments but currently running requests will still hit those nodes.

carlos (sre): do both: flip flag now, then start rollback so traffic drains gracefully. also add temporary routing rule to send existing canary traffic to fallback pool.

sara (oncall): james please flip kill-switch. I'll call the rollback once flag is set.

james (infra): running `flagctl`...

deploy-bot: feature flag `rollout/model_v4_2_0_enabled` set to `false` by james at 2723456812.

emily (support): confirmed no new canary assignments since flag flip. customer tickets stop increasing.

sara (oncall): initiating rollback to v4.1.9 now. li, coordinate validation checks post-rollback.

li (ml): starting rollback: `redwoodctl model rollback --model-name redwood-llm --to-version v4.1.9 --env prod` 

deploy-bot: rollback job 8f3c started on 3 instances. expected duration ~90s.

james (infra): routing change: diverting existing canary sessions to stable pool. command: `routerctl set-route /models/redwood-llm canary -> stable`

carlos (sre): watching metrics: 5xxs on canary nodes dropping. latency normalizing.

li (ml): decode errors stop appearing in logs on nodes that got rolled back. validating with smoke tests: running small prompt set.

li (ml): smoke tests passed against v4.1.9. outputs look good. tokenizer is tok-v1 as expected.

anya (pm): status update for customers: we stopped rollout, rolled back, investigating root cause. ETA for detailed incident report 2h.

emily (support): I'll update ticket #5421: "We've stopped the rollout and rolled back to the previous model. We're investigating the root cause and will follow up with a postmortem."

carlos (sre): can we capture exact drift cause? li, any quick hypothesis?

li (ml): preliminary: release pipeline had incorrect artifact tag mapping — model weights bundle for v4.2.0 were built against tokenizer tok-v2, but the deployment config for canary omitted the tokenizer artifact, so runtime fell back to prod default tok-v1. mismatch surfaced only when canary nodes used mixed artifact sets. root cause likely release packaging bug in `build-release.sh` where `--include-tokenizer` flag was accidentally removed in a refactor.

james (infra): I will pin deploy pipeline to block when tokenizer artifact missing. adding a preflight check: `ci/checks/verify-tokenizer-artifact.sh` to release job.

sara (oncall): incident state: mitigated. actions taken: kill-switch flipped, rollback to v4.1.9, routing diverted. No broad customer impact reported, isolated canary-only.

pagerduty-bot: incident INC-2026-324 status updated to RESOLVED by sara at 2723457300.

anya (pm): follow-ups: - postmortem doc (owner: li) - CI pipeline preflight (owner: james) - improve deploy logs to include tokenizer artifact hash (owner: sara) - customer comms update (owner: emily).

li (ml): I'll start the postmortem draft and include a minimal repro + the offending commit hash.

emily (support): sending customer update now.

carlos (sre): closing monitoring loop: alert thresholds tuned so that small canary noise won't auto-page unless signature matches decode_error pattern.

sara (oncall): handing off to li for postmortem. I'll stay on standby for 30m then sign off. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

li (ml): handover acknowledged. I'll post the postmortem link here when ready.

deploy-bot: logs archived to s3://redwood-incidents/INC-2026-324/logs.tar.gz

emily (support): ticket #5421 updated and closed after confirmation from customer.

sara (oncall): last check: metrics steady, no new reports. marking incident mitigated at 2723457389.
